samarco-fundao-dam-mariana.whole: In 2014, the last full year before the collapse, Samarco produced 25.1 million tonnes of iron ore pellets and fines and sold 25.1 million tonnes, almost all of it exported. It reported net revenue of R$7.54 billion, net income of R$2.81 billion and R$597.7 million paid in taxes and charges, with 2,969 employees and about 3,500 contractors. These are the company's own figures; no independent check was found.

mag-silver-cascabel-solorio-killings.whole: The project never went past exploration. MAG Silver's first independent estimate for the Cinco de Mayo property put inferred resources at 12.45 million tonnes grading 132 g/t silver, 2.86% lead and 6.47% zinc. Drilling stopped after the Benito Juárez ejido voted on 17 November 2012 to expel the company; MAG said work would resume only once it had a land-use permit, drill permits and an access agreement with the ejido (MAG Silver, April 2013). jordan-fuel-protests-2012.whole: The fuel price rise came under a 36-month IMF Stand-By Arrangement of about $2 billion, approved on 3 August 2012. In November 2014 the IMF said the losses of the state electricity company were higher than expected because of gas supply shortfalls, and waived a missed deficit target. At the final review in July 2015 the IMF said inflation was low, reserves adequate and the current account deficit narrowing, but growth had slowed in the first quarter of 2015 and public debt was only 'expected to start stabilizing' that year. These are the IMF's own assessments; no independent evaluation was found.

In 2020 the economy shrank 8.2%, public debt rose from 72% to 87% and unemployment reached 16.2% (Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung).

He said Savia had invested about $2.6 billion since 2009, drilled 190 development and 28 exploration wells, and brought the Peruvian state about $1.1 billion in income. These are the company's own figures; no independent check was found.

hydro-alunorte-barcarena-2018.whole: After the February 2018 flooding, Brazilian authorities limited Alunorte to 50% of capacity, and its alumina output for 2018 was 3.7 million tonnes. Hydro set a target of 7.0 million tonnes a year by 2021. It estimated the investments, costs and fines under September 2018 agreements at about R$360 million; separately, it committed R$100 million over 10 years to local projects and listed R$675 million of wastewater investments. These are Hydro's own figures; no independent check was found.

benetton-mapuche-cushamen.whole: When the Benetton family bought Compañía de Tierras Sud Argentino in 1991, it held about 360,000 hectares in Chubut and Río Negro, including the Leleque and Maitén estates. Its Patagonian operation runs about 250,000 sheep and produces more than 880,000 kilos of wool. In November 2026 Benetton sold its more than 900,000 hectares in Argentina to Adecoagro partners for an undisclosed price (Buenos Aires Times).

By Solway's own count, on an undated web page, it produces over 1,000 tonnes of nickel in ferronickel a month, aims for over 20,000 tonnes a year, employs 1,936 people, and Solway has invested almost $620 million since 2011. In 2014 the plan was 25,000 tonnes of ferronickel a year (BNamericas). No independent check of these figures was found.

In 2007 three districts held non-binding referenda and most voters opposed the mine, and in early 2009 the company missed its deadline to file the environmental impact assessment (Oxfam America, 2009).

The Canadian Press reported Blackfire's president Brent Willis as saying many residents valued the jobs and local business it brought but gave no numbers; no independent check was found (Canadian Press, December 2009, via Mines and Communities).

Coca-Cola's public relations director said 34% of its Colombian workforce was unionised, against 4% of workers nationally. No figures on output, jobs or taxes were found, and no independent check of the union figure (Lapan, UC Berkeley CLAS, 2006).

xolobeni-titanium-rhadebe.whole: No mine was built and no mining right was granted. Transworld Energy and Resources, in which Australia's Mineral Commodities (MRC) held an interest, applied for a mining right in March 2015, and in 2016 MRC announced it would divest from the project (Engineering News). In 2019 Mineral Resources Minister Gwede Mantashe said any licence would depend on MRC's compliance at its Tormin mine; no figures on the deposit or promised jobs were given (City Press).

dar-es-salaam-water.whole: City Water was meant to put capital into the system but injected only about half of what it should have, US$8.5 million, alongside US$40 million in construction contracts that started late. It stopped paying its monthly lease fee in January 2004, and its revenue fell by a third between August 2003 and March 2005. Under the public company DAWASCO, water lost before billing fell from as much as 76% to about 56.5% in 2009, connections rose 12.7% from 2006 to 2009, and metered users rose from 45% to 67% (Pigeon, Municipal Services Project).

mopani-mufulira.whole: In January 2021 Glencore's subsidiary Carlisa agreed to sell its 90% of Mopani to Zambia's state-owned ZCCM for $1, with Mopani keeping $1.5 billion of debt owed to Glencore companies. The debt is to be repaid from a share of Mopani's revenue and earnings, and Glencore keeps the right to buy Mopani's copper until it is paid off (Engineering News). No figures on Mopani's copper output, jobs or taxes were found.

manila-water-concessions.whole: In the east zone, the share of people with 24-hour water rose from 26% in 1997 to over 95% by 2006, and water lost to leaks and theft fell from 63% to about 30%. Manila Water added about 141,000 households (850,000 people), served about 600,000 households in all, and had invested over P17 billion by 2005. These figures were reported by the Philippine Star and appear to come from the company; no independent check was found.

buenos-aires-aguas-argentinas.whole: From 1993 to 2002, water coverage rose from 70% to 79% against a target of 88%, and sewer coverage from 58% to 63% against a target of 74%. The regulator ETOSS estimated Aguas Argentinas met 60.9% of its investment targets, only 2.6% of its investment came from its own funds, and it met 7% of the original sewage treatment targets. The average home tariff rose 87.9% from 1993 to 2002 while consumer prices rose 7.3%, and the company earned an average profit of over 20% on net assets in 1994-2001 (Azpiazu and Castro, Municipal Services Project).

mozambique-cashew.whole: After the export ban was lifted, the real price paid to farmers nearly doubled between 1990/91 and 1999/00 before falling sharply in 2000/01, and farmers' share of the export price rose from about 25% to about 45%. Marketed output averaged 44,300 tonnes, about 10,000 tonnes above the previous decade but half the rise the World Bank projected. Of about $13.5 million a year in gains, farmers got about $5.3 million and traders and exporters about $8.2 million, while the government gained about $2 million a year in export tax (McMillan, Rodrik and Welch, CEPR 2002).

haiti-rice-tariff.whole: Haiti cut its rice tariff from 50% to 3% in 1995, and annual imports immediately rose by more than 60,000 tonnes to 207,000 tonnes. Rice's share of daily calories in Haiti grew from 7% in 1985 to 23% in 2011, while local yields averaged 1.83 tonnes per hectare over the past decade and domestic output trended slightly down (USDA Economic Research Service, 2016).

jamaica-dairy-imports.whole: Jamaica's fresh milk output peaked at 38.8 million litres in 1992 and fell to 12.2 million litres in 2010 and 12.34 million in 2013. The dairy herd fell about 33% after 2004 to about 12,400 head. The government's 2014 dairy paper named imports in a market distorted by subsidies in exporting countries, along with energy costs, cattle theft and costly imported inputs (Jamaica Ministry Paper 54, 2014).

bujagali.whole: The 250 MW run-of-river plant has supplied about 45% of Uganda's annual electricity generation since 2012. Its tariff was 11.3 US cents per kWh in 2017 and was set to rise to 14.7 cents by 2023; in July 2018 more than $400 million of its loans were refinanced and the repayment date moved from 2023 to 2032 to lower the tariff. Before it opened, the government spent about $180 million a year on tariff subsidies, which Bujagali reduced (International Energy Agency).

polonoroeste.whole: Paving of the BR-364 highway was finished quickly, but the programme's environmental and Indigenous protection parts lagged behind, which a 1984 midterm review blamed on weak coordination and inefficient institutions. Brazil's own share of the cost was about $1 billion, beside about $500 million in World Bank loans. Cleared forest in Rondônia grew from 4,200 km² in 1978 to 30,000 km² in 1988 and 48,648 km² in 1996, about 20% of the state's original forest (World Bank, Mahar and Ducrot, 1998).

transmigration-indonesia.whole: From 1950 to 1986 the programme moved 698,200 families, about 3.5 million people, mostly to Sumatra; the 1989-1994 plan aimed for another 550,000 families. The World Bank acknowledged that hoped-for gains in household income from cash crops had not been met, and a survey by a French consultant found 80% of sites failed to improve settlers' living standards (Multinational Monitor, 1990).

chad-cameroon-pipeline.whole: Chad's government revenue rose from about $112 million in 2000 to over $2 billion in 2008, almost 90% of it from oil. In 2007 about 58% of spending went to the agreed priority sectors, against a target of 70%. The World Bank's own evaluators rated the overall programme 'unsatisfactory', found poverty trends were not adequately monitored, noted that infant and child mortality rose, and found Chad's governance indicators worsened from 2000 to 2007 (World Bank IEG, 2009).

oruja-rock-soroti.whole: NERAMP is a $243.8 million project, approved in April 2014, to rehabilitate the 340 km Tororo-Kamdini road corridor. As of January 2022 major rehabilitation had not started because of delays in designs, safeguards documents and finding sources of aggregate, though emergency works on the Lira-Kamdini section were approved in March 2021. The Bank says the finished road would serve over 2.25 million people (World Bank FAQ, 2022). These are the Bank's own statements; no independent check was found.

sources_add.title: FAQ: Uganda North Eastern Road-Corridor Asset Management Project

teresina-lagoas-do-norte.whole: About 100,000 people live in the Lagoas do Norte area, 65% on roughly $1.5 a day. By 2013 the first phase had worked on 325 of the 1,300 hectares needing recovery, moved 400 families out of flood-risk zones, and given 253 brick-making families compensation, pensions or retraining; an additional financing of up to $120 million was planned (World Bank, 2013). These are the Bank's own figures; no independent check was found.
teresina-lagoas-do-norte.searched: World Bank Oct 2013 feature on Lagoas do Norte results

sources_add.title: Teresina: Lagoas do Norte recovery results

serbia-social-card.whole: The World Bank approved the €82.6 million Public Sector Efficiency and Green Recovery development policy loan on 29 April 2021. It backed reforms in public procurement, public hiring, management of social protection programmes, state aid control, air pollution and a legal framework for climate policy, and was meant to speed Serbia's recovery from COVID-19 (World Bank). These are the Bank's stated aims; no results data were found.

sources_add.title: World Bank Supports Serbia's Move Toward Greener, More Resilient and Inclusive Growth

dakar-brt-grand-medine.whole: Dakar's BRT opened on 15 January 2024 with 18.3 km of reserved lanes, 23 stops across 14 municipalities and 121 electric buses. It was designed to carry 300,000 passengers, and the trip on the line was cut from about 90 to 45 minutes. It cost 419 billion CFA francs (about €680 million), financed by the World Bank, the European Investment Bank and the Green Climate Fund (Afrik21, 2024). No ridership figures since opening were found.

sources_add.title: Senegal: the long-awaited solar-powered Dakar BRT finally goes into service

ibadan-flood-channel.whole: By mid-2024 the project had disbursed $147.1 million of its $200 million. The World Bank reported 13.3 of 18.4 km of channel works complete in one package and 13.6 of 13.9 km in another, 37 culverts and bridges rehabilitated, the Eleyele dam rehabilitated, 430 km of natural channels dredged, and 5 weather stations and 11 sirens installed. These are the Bank's own figures from a restructuring paper, with no independent check found; no figures on people protected or flood outcomes were given.

sources_add.title: Ibadan Urban Flood Management Project (P130840) Restructuring Paper

jharkhand-santhal-water-plant.whole: The World Bank approved a $500 million IDA credit in January 2014 for rural water and sanitation in Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh, starting in 33 districts. It funds mostly single-village groundwater schemes, multi-village schemes where local water is unsuitable, drains and soak-pits, and pilots of 24/7 and solar-powered supply, and was expected to benefit about 7.8 million rural people. These are the Bank's stated aims; no results data were found.

sources_add.title: World Bank press release on rural water supply and sanitation in four Indian states (7 January 2014)

webuye-interchange-traders.whole: The World Bank approved $300 million in April 2011 for the Kenya Transport Sector Support Project, covering about 221 km of roads including upgrading of the Kisumu-Kakamega-Webuye-Kitale route, sections of the Northern Corridor, and the Mombasa airport runway. Its aims were to ease bottlenecks on transit traffic and trade in western Kenya and to raise aviation safety. These are the Bank's stated aims; no results data were found.

sources_add.title: World Bank press release on $300 million to upgrade 221 km of roads and improve air transport in Kenya (21 April 2011)

proroutes-bukavu-goma.whole: ProRoutes is backed by $238 million in IDA credits in all. By the World Bank's count, since 2008 it has reopened more than 2,300 km of roads and maintains 3,000 km of high-priority national roads in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Bukavu-Goma road was one of three new sections funded by additional financing approved in February 2016; no figures on travel times or people served were given (World Bank factsheet, 2018). These are the Bank's own figures; no independent check was found.
proroutes-bukavu-goma.searched: World Bank Sept 2018 ProRoutes AF2 factsheet

sources_add.title: Democratic Republic of Congo: High-Priority Reopening and Maintenance of Roads Project, Second Additional Financing (ProRoutes AF2)

kamwenge-fort-portal-road.whole: The 66 km Fort Portal-Kamwenge road was completed by China Railway Seventh Group and commissioned by President Museveni in September 2017 at a cost of $33.3 million. After the World Bank withdrew, Uganda's government paid the rest. Expected benefits named were access to rural centres, tourism at Kibale National Park, farming and mining areas, and links to the Northern Corridor and Congo (Construction Review Online, 2017).
kamwenge-fort-portal-road.searched: Construction Review Online Sept 2017 on commissioning

sources_add.title: Uganda commissions 66km Fort Portal-Kamwenge road

vishnugad-pipalkoti-haat.whole: In 2015 the developer, THDC India, was scheduled to finish the $922 million plant by December 2017 (Renewable Energy World). A World Bank restructuring paper from about mid-2022 put civil works at over 33% complete, 58% of the main equipment delivered, disbursements of $165.97 million, 37% of the loan, in the text ($172.68 million in its finance table), against a net loan commitment of $448 million, and first-unit commissioning postponed to June 2024, citing poor geology and COVID-19. Once finished it is meant to produce 1,665 GWh a year; this is a design figure, not output. These are the World Bank's own figures; no independent check was found.
vishnugad-pipalkoti-haat.searched: Renewable Energy World Aug 2015; World Bank restructuring paper RES51825 (c. 2022)

sources_add.title: Progress continues at 444-MW Vishnugad Pipalkoti hydroelectric project
Vishnugad Pipalkoti Hydro Electric Project (P096124) Restructuring Paper RES51825

giza-north-groundwater.whole: By the World Bank's count, the gas-fired combined-cycle plant was connected to the grid in 2015 after four years of construction, adding 2,250 MW, about 8% of Egypt's available capacity, enough for more than five million homes. The Bank lent $600 million in 2010 and $240 million in 2012, alongside the European Investment Bank and the OPEC Fund. These are the Bank's own figures; no independent check was found.
giza-north-groundwater.searched: World Bank Dec 2015 feature story on Egypt's added capacity

sources_add.title: Egypt's extra electricity to power more than five million households

lbod-tidal-link-badin.whole: LBOD was built from 1985 to 1997 to drain about 530,000 hectares in Nawabshah, Sanghar and Mirpurkhas districts, at a cost of $605.3 million by WAPDA's count, aiming to raise cropping intensity from 81% to 147%. In one surveyed Mirpurkhas area of 466 hectares with tile drainage, cropping intensity rose from 37% to 86% and wheat yields from 878 to 2,257 kg per hectare between 1994/95 and 1997/98, with a benefit-cost ratio of 1.26 (Memon, Osanami and Kondo, Hokkaido University, 2001).
lbod-tidal-link-badin.searched: Hokkaido University impact study (2001); Dawn 2006 on Inspection Panel findings

wagp-badagry.whole: Ghana's contract was for 120 million standard cubic feet of gas a day through the pipeline, but in 2016 deliveries averaged about 30 million a day. A Volta River Authority source blamed pipeline vandalism in Nigeria rather than Ghana's arrears, and the Africa Centre for Energy Policy urged Ghana to find other suppliers (Ecofin Agency, March 2016).

naso-san-san-druy.whole: The Naso territory the project was meant to demarcate was created by law as the Naso Tjër Di comarca on 4 December 2020, after Panama's Supreme Court ruled on 12 November 2020 that the government must secure Indigenous peoples' collective access to ancestral lands. It covers about 1,600 km² for a Naso nation of around 4,000 people (Mongabay, 2021). No figures on what the World Bank project itself delivered were found.
naso-san-san-druy.searched: Mongabay Feb 2021 on comarca recognition; no project completion report found

ijora-oloye-lagos-1998.searched: World Bank project page and IEG search results (pages found were for other Nigerian projects); no completion report for the Lagos Drainage and Sanitation Project opened

planafloro-rondonia.whole: The Inspection Panel's 1997 review credited Bank assistance with 'significant improvements' in the project's technical and accounting administration. It found zoning and funding for protected areas delayed, forest clearing still near 450,000 hectares a year, continued illegal logging and settlement in protected areas, and limited progress on an Indigenous health plan. Local people still said continuing the project was better than ending Bank involvement (World Bank Inspection Panel, 1997).
planafloro-rondonia.searched: Inspection Panel news page on its 1997 Planafloro review

sources_add.title: Inspection Panel finds mixed results in Brazilian Amazon project

codevi-ouanaminthe.whole: In 2018 more than 11,000 Haitians worked at the CODEVI free zone, over 20% of Haiti's 52,950 textile jobs, and its president Fernando Capellán said he planned 25,000 jobs by 2020 (HaitiLibre, December 2018). HaitiLibre did not name the source of the job figures; no independent check was found.
codevi-ouanaminthe.searched: HaitiLibre Dec 2018; Le Nouvelliste headline citing 20,000 jobs not opened

sources_add.title: Haiti - Economy: A Dominican responsible for more than 20% of textile jobs in the country

agilis-kiryandongo.whole: Agilis's Joseph Initiative buys from a network of 15,000 smallholder farmers, 3,400 of whom were trained in the previous year, and Kiryandongo's resident district commissioner said yields rose from about five bags of maize an acre to 8-10 bags (The Independent, Uganda). No figures on the farm's own output, jobs or investment were found, and no independent check of these figures.

aperam-jequitinhonha.whole: Aperam BioEnergia holds about 124,000 hectares in the upper Jequitinhonha valley, 66% of it FSC-certified eucalyptus, and produces 427,200 tonnes of charcoal a year, with plans for 539,000 tonnes by 2033. The IFC's 2024 €250 million sustainability-linked loan to Aperam was to fund buying 42,600 more hectares, more charcoal capacity, more efficient kilns and a bio-oil business (Early Warning System, from IFC disclosure). These are the company's and lender's figures; no independent check was found.

ndayane-port.whole: DP World's Ndayane port is a $1.1 billion project under two 25-year concessions signed with Senegal in 2020, which the Maritime Executive called the largest single private investment in Senegal's history. Phase 1, about $837 million, is to add 1.2 million TEU a year of container capacity with a 2,750-foot quay; full completion was expected in 2026 (Maritime Executive, January 2022). No figures on operations or jobs were found.
ndayane-port.searched: Maritime Executive Jan 2022 on construction start

sources_add.title: DP World Starts Construction of a $1.1 Billion Port in Senegal

shuakhevi-adjaristsqali.whole: The scheme pairs the 178 MW Shuakhevi plant with the 9 MW Skhalta plant. Commercial operation began in 2017, but about 300 of roughly 38,000 metres of diversion tunnels failed soon after, which the designer blamed on water interacting with the surrounding rock; after repairs it was planned to restart at 50% capacity in early 2020 and run fully by spring 2020. The owner, Adjaristsqali Georgia, is co-owned by Clean Energy Invest, Tata Power and the IFC, with EBRD and ADB funding (CBW, Georgia, c. 2019). No generation figures were found.
shuakhevi-adjaristsqali.searched: CBW (Georgia) article c. 2019 on restart; Bankwatch pages not opened

sources_add.title: Shuakhevi HPP to start electricity production in 2020

wings-long-beluah.whole: IFC's 2012 disclosure described a $176 million Wings Group project, with IFC loans of up to $88 million to four Wings companies. The CAO found PT Inti Selaras Perkasa, the plantation at Long Beluah, was not financed by the IFC; the link was that up to 1.6% of an IFC-backed Wings company's raw materials came from its parent plantation group. The plantation began sending fruit to a mill in 2013 (CAO assessment, 2019). No output or job figures were found.

sources_add.title: CAO Assessment Report: Wings-01, Indonesia

mhp-vinnytsia-poultry.whole: MHP finished the second stage of its Vinnytsia complex in 2019, adding 260,000 tonnes of poultry meat to its production at an estimated cost of about $420 million, and expected the site to run at full capacity by the end of 2021, taking the company's total capacity to about 840,000 tonnes a year by 2022 (Just Food, April 2019). These are company figures; no independent check was found.
mhp-vinnytsia-poultry.searched: Just Food April 2019 on Vinnytsia expansion

sources_add.title: Ukraine's MHP completes poultry plant expansion

alto-maipo.whole: The two run-of-river plants, Alfalfal II and Las Lajas, have 531 MW of capacity; construction ended in December 2021 and all four units were in commercial operation by mid-May 2022. AES Andes put more than $1 billion into construction, and in May 2022 a US court approved a Chapter 11 plan restructuring about $1.8 billion of the project's debt. The expected yearly output was said to be enough for more than a million Chilean homes (Diario Financiero, May 2022).
alto-maipo.searched: Diario Financiero May 2022 on Chapter 11 completion

sources_add.title: Alto Maipo finaliza reestructuración financiera bajo el Capítulo 11 en Estados Unidos

indura-tela-bay.whole: The resort has 60 junior suites in 15 villas and what was billed as Honduras's first championship 18-hole golf course, designed by Gary Player, on 1,800 acres inside Jeannette Kawas National Park. It joined Hilton's Curio Collection in November 2016; its owner, Desarrollo Turístico Bahía de Tela, includes the Honduran tourism investment fund FHIT (Hilton press release via Hospitality Net, 2016). These are the owner's and Hilton's own descriptions; no figures on investment, jobs or visitors, and no independent check, were found.

sources_add.title: Curio – A Collection by Hilton Debuts Five-Star Beach & Golf Resort in Honduras
